# Develop RN App

The SeaTalk RN team will be providing an SDK comprising of various packages focusing on different aspects of functionality. Please refer to our API docs for all the packages provided.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Most of the packages are recommended for the purpose of keeping our user's experience consistent with the rest of the SeaTalk app. For example, we strongly recommend to use UI widgets defined in our`@seatalk-rn/sdk-widgets`package. However, with that said, we do allow implementing your own UI components when necessary.

## Naming Convention

We adopt a scope of`@seatalk-rn`to our package naming. SDK packages will have`@seatalk-rn/sdk-`prefix while application packages can be named anything with prefix`@seatalk-rn`. Please keep your package name lowercase of course.

# Development Environment

SeaTalk RN SDK provides two environments, namely test and live. You may switch the environment following the procedure below:

## For iOS

1. Overturn your SeaTalk Dev app to bring up the**Forbidden Zone**page
2. Tap the**Servers**section and choose one of the presets.

   |SeaTalk Server Environment|SeaTalk RN Environment|
   |---|---|
   |Test|test|
   |Dev1, Dev2, Dev3, Dev4|test|
   |Live Staging|live|
   |Live|live|

## For Android

1. **Overturn your phone**while in SeaTalk app or use**command(⌘)+M**(for emulator) shortcut to bring up the**Debug View**page
2. Tap the**"Server"**entry
3. Select the server referencing the following table:

   |SeaTalk Server Environment|SeaTalk RN Environment|
   |---|---|
   |test (20443)|test|
   |Dev1 (21443), Dev2 (22443), Dev3 (23443), Dev4 (24443)|test|
   |Live Staging (1443)|live|
   |Live (443)|live|
4. After selecting a server, you will be logged out automatically and please log in again.

# Preview Development Bundle

**Note**: Do not confuse the steps here with the remote loading approach in [Test RN App](/docs/get-leave-balance-report_test-rn-app). The procedure described below is for app developers to use the utilities provided by React Native during active development, while remote loading is for QAs to test the apps as if they are downloaded from SeaTalk Open Platform.You may load your JS bundle in the SeaTalk App following the procedure below:

## For iOS

1. Overturn your SeaTalk Dev app to bring up the**Forbidden Zone**page
2. Turn on the Switch for the "**\[RN\] Enable Dev**" section
3. Go into the "**\[RN\] Dev Bundle**" setting page and type in the bundle URL and entry module. Tap the "**Load Application**" button.
4. Go back to Forbidden Zone page and tap the "**\[RN\] Show**" to view your page.
5. Switch off the "**\[RN\] Enable Dev**" when no longer needed.

## For Android

1. **Overturn your phone**while in SeaTalk app or use**command(⌘)+M**(for emulator) shortcut to bring up the**Debug View**page
2. Tap the**React Native**entry
3. To load the development bundle served from the computer, you need to turn on the React Native debug mode, by turning on switch to the right of**Enable Dev Mode**
4. Enter the**App ID**and**Entry Module**of the development bundle, which should be registered in the JS code
5. Tap**Start RN Activity**to launch the RN page
6. In the RN activity,**shake the mobile device**or use**command(⌘)+**M (for emulator) to invoke the**RN debug menu**
7. Under**Change Bundle Location**, enter the URL where the bundle is served. E.g. if the bundle is served at`http://localhost:8081/dist/index.bundle`, you should enter`localhost:8081/dist`.
8. We currently only support using`index`as the bundle name
9. RN will append the correct query parameters
10. You might need to execute`adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081`if you are connecting the phone via USB and using`localhost`
11. If you are loading a different bundle, you might need to tap**Reload RN**in the**\[DEV\] React Native**page, as well as**Reload**in the**RN debug menu**.

# Show the App on SeaTalk Mobile App

Getting your app shown up in discover page is completely SeaTalk logic. We have our own permission control system. As an application developer, you may not need to concern about this.
